messages:
kai (eng-runtime): Heads up — noticed a slow memory growth pattern on long-context runs when comparing Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private. Dedicated shows ~30MB/min growth after ~2k tokens, Hosted stays flat. Can we sanity-check config drift?
anna (eng-runtime): interesting. What kernel/driver combos are those Dedicated boxes on? Any NVLink differences or custom kube flags?
miguel (eng-runtime): Dedicated is on onprem-like nodes (A100s, driver 525.x) with kernel 5.15 fallback. Hosted uses 6.x kernel on cloud images. Private (VPC) was a mix; one customer reported more paging.
rachel (eng-sre): perf-bot just flagged a regression: kv-cache-evict-rate up 2.3x on a subset of Dedicated hosts. Logged under perf-2212.
perf-bot: Alert: kv_cache:evict_rate increased by 2.3x across hosts in pool redwood-dedicated-1 between 2025-11-05T12:30:00Z and 2025-11-05T12:45:00Z. Top signals: pagefault_count, slab_reclaim, cgroup_mem_pressure.
kai (eng-runtime): Thanks. I captured trace profiles — attaching snippet from pprof (summary):
```
heap_alloc_delta: +180MB over 20m
kv_pages_in_use: +12k frames
pagefaults/sec: 85 -> 240
```
Seems tied to a kernel page-scanner behavior that ramps reclaim under moderate write churn.
anna (eng-runtime): Could be that our jemalloc config on Dedicated enables background purge differently. Any differences in MALLOC_CONF or MALLOC_ARENA?
miguel (eng-runtime): We do set MALLOC_CONF=“dirty_decay_ms:50000,muzzy_decay_ms:50000,background_thread:true” on Dedicated for throughput. Hosted defaults to cloud distro (background_thread:false). That could affect fragmentation over long-lived KV slabs.
kai (eng-runtime): Nice catch. Also batching heuristics matter: Dedicated had aggressive batch size=64 for cost-optim, which keeps KV cache pinned longer and delays prefix eviction, increasing working set. Hosted uses batch size auto=latency-first so smaller batches.
rachel (eng-sre): Operational constraints in VPC (Private) mean we disabled cgroup swap and limited swappiness, which changed page reclaim patterns. Customer reported more frequent small evictions (higher fragmentation).
anna (eng-runtime): Action items I propose: 1) run a controlled A/B on one Dedicated rack toggling MALLOC_CONF background_thread off vs on, 2) run same long-context test with batch_size=16 vs 64, 3) enable kernel tunables (vm.swappiness=10) on a test Private node to see impact.
miguel (eng-runtime): I can run 1 and 2 on a staging rack. Quick repro script I used:
```
# generate long-context workload
for i in {1..100}; do echo "prompt" >> prompts.txt; done
time ./inference_client --model rwd-13b --batch_size 64 --context 8192 --requests 200
```
Capture /proc/vmstat and perf counters during run.
kai (eng-runtime): Also add nvml logs — on Dedicated the driver fallback triggers a kernel ABI shim sometimes which changes page cache alignment.
rachel (eng-sre): I'll open a privileged runbook for the Dedicated nodes and snapshot current sysctl and MALLOC_CONF. Keep me posted before any change.
anna (eng-runtime): If experiments show background_thread is the culprit, we should add a default MALLOC profile per deployment type and surface it in Console (Optimize -> runtime recommendations).
miguel (eng-runtime): Starting A/B now on staging-02 (dedicated). Will post perf graphs in ~30m.
kai (eng-runtime): Great. If we see fragmentation instead of steady growth, we might want to tweak the KV page reclamation heuristic to prioritize older frames for eviction. I'll draft a small allocator patch to prefer LRU-age over in-use-count.
anna (eng-runtime): small reminder: keep tests short and instrument token-level timings so we don't conflate latency regressions with background GC.
rachel (eng-sre): Perf run scheduled. perf-bot will post final summary.
perf-bot: Summary (staging-02, batch_size=64, background_thread:on): mem_growth: +28MB/min, evict_rate: high, pagefaults spike at 2k tokens. (next run with background_thread:off queued)
